ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r1.claim: Balad warned Quraysh that Makkah’s prosperity came through Abraham’s prayer and the House, so they must not become arrogant; Shams warns what follows if they persist.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r1.anchor: warned of their fate should they persist in their arrogance

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r3.claim: The soul mirrors the larger world: God inspires good and evil, inclines it to good and against evil, and requires it to preserve balance; unchecked evil leads to arrogance and disorder.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r3.anchor: inclined it towards good and made it hate evil

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r1.claim: The soul itself witnesses its Maker’s purpose: awareness of good and evil entails adopting good and avoiding evil; success is purification and failure is sin, so denying accountability contradicts this witness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r1.anchor: the awareness of good and evil is found in it. Obviously, the reason for giving him this awareness is that man should adopt good and shield himself from evil

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r2.claim: Because al-nafs lacks the definite article, it can convey magnitude, multitude, or scarcity; Islahi prefers magnitude to highlight the soul’s remarkable wisdom and abilities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r2.anchor: In my opinion, here it connotes magnitude

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r3.claim: Mā sawwāhā is also a verbal noun pointing to the soul’s artistry; such a highly endowed creation must have a purpose and face accountability.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r4.claim: Taswiyah denotes creation’s final stage, as in 87:2; the perfected soul’s capacities make it a witness that humans have responsibilities and answer to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p334/r4.anchor: here it is not merely the initial stage of the creation of the human soul which is referred to in this oath, its final stage is also in consideration

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r1.claim: God placed a divine spark in each person that enables discernment between good and evil.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r1.anchor: It is this divine spark which enables a person to discern good from evil.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r4.claim: Using every divine favour rightly serves one’s own interest and expresses gratitude; failing to do so is self-destruction.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r4.anchor: every favour God has bestowed on him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r5.claim: As a person who closes his eyes risks falling and bears responsibility, a person must stay alert to the moral path he follows.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p335/r5.anchor: there is a strong probability that he might fall in a pit and he himself would be responsible for this mishap and no other person.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r1.claim: The oath by the human soul makes its own nature evidence: God’s inborn awareness of good and evil entails success for good and a dreadful fate for evil.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r1.anchor: The third oath is sworn by the way human soul has been formed which occupies the status of evidence borne by man’s inner self.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r3.claim: Suppressing the complement lets everything evident from the oaths count as its content; one prominent implication is that God destroys rebellious nations.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r3.anchor: The benefit of this suppression is that everything

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r6.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وأبو عبيدة والطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r6.claim: They take mā as a relative pronoun, preferred by al-Ṭabarī, because mā can refer to rational and nonrational beings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r6.anchor: وما في قوله: وما بناها، وما طحاها، وما سواها، بمعنى الذي، قاله الحسن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r7.speaker: قتادة والمبرد والزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r7.claim: Qatada, al-Mubarrad, and al-Zajjāj take mā as an infinitive, consistent with their view that it does not refer individually to rational beings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r7.anchor: وقيل: مصدرية، قاله قتادة والمبرد والزجاج،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī rejects the infinitive reading because of فألهمها and prefers a relative meaning like the powerful builder and wise maker.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r8.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: جعلت مصدرية، وليس بالوجه لقوله: فألهمها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r9.claim: The author replies that an infinitive mā is sound: the pronoun in فألهمها can return to God understood from context, and no syntactic corruption follows.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r9.anchor: ولا يلزم ذلك لأنا إذا جعلناها مصدرية عاد الضمير على ما يفهم من سياق الكلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r10.claim: Mā and man are both unable to function as descriptive adjectives, so this gives no basis for preferring mā over man.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p486/r10.anchor: وقوله إنما أوثرت إلخ لا يراد بما ولا بمن الموصولتين معنى الوصفية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r9.claim: The outward cosmos has an inward human counterpart, so celestial and terrestrial features can be read as faculties and bodily processes.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r9.anchor: وليس في العالم الآفاقي شيء إلا وفي العالم النفساني نظيره

BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r10.claim: The seven heavens correspond to layers of the head and its cognitive and sensory faculties; the sun is spirit, night temperament, day heart, and moon soul.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r10.anchor: فالسماوات سبع كطباق الرأس التي تتعلق بالقوى المعنوية والحسية كالذاكرة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r11.claim: Inner organs resemble stars; rain, heat, cold, thunder, lightning, and winds correspond respectively to tears, grief, joy, speech, salt, and breath.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r11.anchor: والأمطار كالدمع , والحر كالحزن , والبرد كالسرور , والرعد كالنطق , والبرق كالملح

BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r12.claim: The lower world’s seven layers correspond to body layers; mountains resemble bones, and minerals and waters resemble bodily fluids and excretions.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r12.anchor: والعالم السفلي سبع طباق أيضا , قال الملوي : ( ونظيرها طبقة الجلد )

BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r13.claim: Vegetation resembles hair, while animals and birds resemble lice and fleas; the body’s front is inhabited and its back ruined.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r13.anchor: والنبات كالشعور تارة تحلق كالحصاد وتارة تقلع كالنتف

BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r14.claim: The soul is the cosmos’s most wondrous and comprehensive feature, balanced from discordant mixtures into a harmonized whole.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r14.anchor: ولما كانت النفوس أعجب ما في الكون وأجمع , عبر فيها بالتسوية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r15.claim: The oath’s implied conclusion is that God gave souls differing dispositions and capacity for purification or corruption, urging people to purify themselves in view of resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p438/r15.anchor: جواب القسم مقدر تقديره : لقد طبع سبحانه وتعالى نفوسكم على طبائع متباينة

NAHHAS:v5p235/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p235/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p235/r8.claim: Sawwāhā means its proportioning; interpreting mā as ‘the one who proportioned it’ would refer to God and require man, not mā.
NAHHAS:v5p235/r8.anchor: أي تسويتها قال أبو جعفر ومن قال المعنى الذي سواها أراد الله جل وعز ولو كان كما قال لكان ومن

DURR-FULL:v8p527/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p527/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p527/r8.claim: He glossed the sun as its light, the moon as following it, daylight as illuminating it, God as builder of heaven, the earth as spread out, inspiration as showing good and evil, and corruption as leading astray.
DURR-FULL:v8p527/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {و الشمس وضحاها}

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p366/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p366/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p366/r1.claim: The oath confirms the threat of destruction implicitly conveyed by the news; each waw following a pause is an oath particle, and the sun, moon, sky, earth, and human soul display God's wise and powerful creation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p366/r1.anchor: القسم لتأكيد الخبر ، والمقصود بالتأكيد هو ما في سوق الخبر من التعريض بالتهديد والوعيد بالاستئصال .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p366/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p366/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p366/r4.claim: The oath is prepared by noting that purifying the soul leads to success, while neglecting its reform leads to immorality and loss.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p366/r4.anchor: ومهد لذلك بالتنبيه على أن تزكية النفس سبب الفلاح ، وأن التقصير في إصلاحها سبب الفجور والخسران .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p368/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p368/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p368/r6.claim: The soul is the human self; its indefinite form denotes the entire kind, as in another verse, and its being made even means created without unevenness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p368/r6.anchor: وتنكير ( نفس ) للنوعية أي جنس النفس فيعم كل نفس عموما بالقرينة على نحو قوله تعالى : { علمت نفس ما قدمت وأخرت }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p368/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p368/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p368/r7.claim: If the three instances of ما are source nouns, the oath is by effects of God's action-attributes: raising the sky, spreading Earth, and shaping the human being.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p368/r7.anchor: إما مصدرية يؤول الفعل بعدها بمصدر فالقسم بأمور من آثار قدرة الله تعالى وهي صفات الفعل الإلاهية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r5.claim: The repeated wāws can govern both accusative and genitive: the oath-wāw omits its verb altogether and substitutes for it, while coordinated wāws inherit that double function, resolving the apparent two-governor problem.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r5.anchor: واو القسم مطرح معها إبراز الفعل إطراحا كليا ، فكان لها شأن خلاف شأن الباء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r6.claim: In وما بناها, وما طحاها, and وما سواها, ما is best taken as a relative pronoun, not a verbal noun, which would spoil the sequence; it means the mighty Creator who built and fashioned them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r6.anchor: جعلت ( ما ) مصدرية في قوله : { وما بناها } { وما طحاها } { وما سواها }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r7.claim: The indefinite نفس may denote Adam specifically, or all souls, left indefinite to convey abundance as in another verse.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r7.anchor: أن يريد نفسا خاصة من بين النفوس وهي نفس آدم

RAZI-FULL:v31p171/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p171/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p171/r1.claim: The sura urges obedience and warns against disobedience; oaths by beneficial created things prompt reflection and gratitude because divine oaths weigh heavily on the heart.
RAZI-FULL:v31p171/r1.anchor: المقصود من هذه السورة الترغيب في الطاعات والتحذير من المعاصي

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:anmerkung/r1.claim: Qur'anic oaths probably draw on a characteristic expression of pre-Islamic soothsayers, though the connection remains insufficiently researched.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zu grundsätzlichen Hinweisen zu den koranischen Schwüren sowie ihrer wahrscheinlichen, aber bis dato noch nicht hinreichend untersuchten Anlehnung an ein charakteristisches Ausdrucksmittel altarabischer Seher

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:anmerkung/r2.claim: The structure and function of cumulative oath series are discussed at 93:1–2, with many parallels.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Zu Aufbau und Funktion ‚akkumulativer Schwurserien’ wie dem vorliegenden Passus s. die Anmerkung zu 93:1.2 mit zahlreichen Parallelstellen

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r1.claim: An eight-verse oath series leads into the antithetical statement in verses 9–10; the pre-Islamic genre is repurposed in verses 5–7 to express biblical creation ideas.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r1.anchor: mit anschließender, antithetischer Schwuraussage (V. 9.10). Die Schwurserie

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r2.claim: The series moves through three complementary or contrasting pairs—sun/moon, night/day, heaven/earth—then the soul, whose opposed moral capacities are specified in verse 8.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r2.anchor: drei aus kontrastierenden bzw. komplementären Elementen aufgebaute Paare (V. 1.2: Sonne und Mond, V. 3.4: Nacht und Tag, V. 5.6: Himmel und Erde)

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r4.claim: The oath series narrows from cosmic creation, traced vertically from celestial bodies to earth, to the human moral subject.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r4.anchor: Zum einen verengt die Serie sukzessive den Fokus von der kosmischen Schöpfungsordnung (die vertikal, von Himmelskörpern bis zur Erde, durchlaufen wird) auf das moralische Subjekt des Menschen

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r5.claim: Its shift from creation to humanity resembles the 81:1–14 sequence, which evokes the world's eschatological dissolution rather than cyclical operation.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r5.anchor: Eine ähnliche Struktur weist etwa auch die ʾiḏā-Serie 81:1–14 auf, wo allerdings die eschatologische Auflösung der Schöpfung und nicht wie in Q 91 ihr zyklisches Funktionieren evoziert wird

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r6.claim: A caesura after verse 4 divides effects and activities of the oath's objects in verses 1–4 from references to God's creating activity in verses 5–8.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r6.anchor: Zum anderen besitzt die Serie eine deutliche Binnenzäsur nach V. 4, die eine Untergliederung in zwei Gesätze nahelegt

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r7.claim: The creator first emerges through indirect, enigmatic mā in the second half of the series; the explicit naming of the Lord in verse 14 resolves the suspense.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r7.anchor: Das dadurch aufgebaute Spannungsmoment löst im Grunde erst die explizite Nennung des „Herrn“ in V. 14 auf

TABATABAI:91:1-8/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:91:1-8/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:91:1-8/r9.claim: The soul and its shaper are sworn by: the shaper has power, knowledge, and wisdom to order its creation and balance its faculties.
TABATABAI:91:1-8/r9.anchor: واقسم بنفس والشيء ذي القدرة والعلم والحكمة الذي سواها

TABATABAI:91:1-8/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:91:1-8/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:91:1-8/r10.claim: Some take the indefinite “soul” as indefinite; others see it as honorific, and the author allows that it may signal that the soul has a distinctive description and significance.
TABATABAI:91:1-8/r10.anchor: وتنكير { نفس } قيل للتنكير، وقيل للتفخيم

TABATABAI:91:1-15/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:91:1-15/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:91:1-15/r2.claim: Al-Qummi glosses the shaping of the soul as its creation and formation.
TABATABAI:91:1-15/r2.anchor: بحث روائي في تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى

TABRISI:91:1-15/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:1-15/r13.speaker: عطاء
TABRISI:91:1-15/r13.claim: The soul may mean all that God created among jinn and humans; al-Hasan instead takes it as Adam and the one who formed him.
TABRISI:91:1-15/r13.anchor: جميع ما خلق من الجن والإنس عن عطاء

TABRISI:91:1-15/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:1-15/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:91:1-15/r14.claim: God fashioned the soul's form and balanced its limbs; another view says intellect distinguishes people from other animals.

THALABI:v10p212#3/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p212#3/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p212#3/r12.claim: God proportioned the soul's creation and inspired it with both wickedness and reverence.
THALABI:v10p212#3/r12.anchor: ونفس وما سواها عدل خلقها فألهمها فجورها وتقواها

THALABI:v10p212#3/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p212#3/r17.speaker: أبو الأسود الدؤلي عن عمران بن حصين
THALABI:v10p212#3/r17.claim: Imran asks whether people's actions are predetermined or arise from prophetic instruction and proof. Abu al-Aswad answers that all is decreed, adding that God created and owns everything and is not questioned while people are.
THALABI:v10p212#3/r17.anchor: عن أبي الأسود الدؤلي قال ب قال لي عمران بن حصين: أرأيت ما يعمل فيه الناس ويتكادحون فيه؟ أشيء قضى عليهم ومضى عليهم من قدر سبق

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r4.claim: The oath by the nafs points to the superiority inherent in human creation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r4.anchor: 7. âyette insan varlığı (nefs) üzerine yemin edilmesi onun yaratılışının özündeki üstünlüğe işaret eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r5.claim: “Fashioning” the soul means placing material and spiritual powers in it, assigning each its function, and giving it organs to use those powers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r5.anchor: “Nefse düzen verme”, ona maddî ve mânevî güçlerin yerleştirilmesi, her gücün yapacağı görevin tayin edilmesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r8.claim: Verses 7–8 summarize humans as morally dual beings created able to choose good or evil, with salvation or ruin depending on that choice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:1/r8.anchor: insanın ahlâkî bakımdan çift kutuplu bir varlık olduğunu, iyilik veya kötülük yollarından dilediğini seçebilecek bir tabiatta yaratıldığını

BURSEVI:v10p342/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p342/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p342/r5.claim: The soul is something God originated and created with readiness for its perfections; the indefinite form magnifies it or denotes the many souls, and may refer to Adam's soul.
BURSEVI:v10p342/r5.anchor: أي ومن أنشأها وأبدعها مستعدة لكملاتها والتنكير للتفخيم

BURSEVI:v10p342/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p342/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p342/r6.claim: Knowledge of the unseen Creator is inferred from the visible world: heaven, earth, and especially ensouled beings, the noblest composite creatures.
BURSEVI:v10p342/r6.anchor: والشاهد ليس إلا العالم الجسماني وهو إما علوي بسيط كالسماء وأما سفلى بسيط كالأرض

QASHANI:91:8/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:91:8/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:91:8/r2.claim: The soul may mean the animal potency impressed in animal spirit, the whole composite, or the rational soul; God balanced it between lordship and lowliness, neither bodily darkness nor spiritual light.
QASHANI:91:8/r2.anchor: القوة الحيوانية المنطبعة في الروح الحيوانية المسماة باصطلاح أهل الشرع والتصوف

QASHANI:91:8/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:91:8/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:91:8/r3.claim: Depending on which soul is meant, its balance is like neither east nor west, a proportioned temperament, or readiness for perfection between the two worlds.
QASHANI:91:8/r3.anchor: عدلها بين جهتي الربوبية والسفالة لا في ظلمة الجسم وكثافته ولا في ضوء الروح ولطافته

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3436#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3436#3/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3436#3/r1.claim: The Prophet says people's deeds are already decreed, yet they work because each person is prepared for the destination for which God created him; he cites the soul and its inspiration toward wickedness and piety.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3436#3/r1.anchor: عن عمران بن حصين : ' ان رجلا قال يا رسول الله : ارايت ما يعمل الناس اليوم ويكدحون فيه شيء قد قضى عليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r6.claim: The phrase fa-sawwāhā forms complete paronomasia with wa-mā sawwāhā earlier in the same surah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r6.anchor: وبين { فسواها } هنا وقوله : { وما سواها } ( الشمس : 7 ) قبله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r6.claim: The sworn-by soul is the human genus; its being fashioned means completing its intellect and discernment, as the following clause explains.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r6.anchor: والنفس التي أقسم بها، اسم الجنس، وتسويتها إكمال عقلها ونظرها،

AKHFASH:v2p580/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p580/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p580/r1.claim: Mā in wa-nafsin wa-mā sawwāhā means the One who fashioned it; God swears by Himself as Lord of the soul He formed, and the oath's answer is qad aflaḥa man zakkāhā.
AKHFASH:v2p580/r1.anchor: فاقسم الله تبارك وتعالى بنفسه وانه رب النفس التي سواها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r1.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وأبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r1.claim: One view takes mā as “who”: “and who built it”; some instead read it as the relative pronoun “that which.” The same two analyses apply to 91:6 and 91:7.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r1.anchor: في ما قولان أحدهما بمعنى من تقديره ومن بناها قاله الحسن ومجاهد وأبو عبيدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r2.speaker: قتادة والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r2.claim: A second view makes mā a verbal noun: “and its building”; this also applies to 91:6 and 91:7.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r2.anchor: والثاني أنها بمعنى المصدر تقديره وبنائها وهذا مذهب قتادة والزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r3.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r3.claim: Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī and others read man instead of mā in all three phrases, “who built/spread/fashioned them.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r3.anchor: وقد قرأ أبو عمران الجوني في آخرين ومن بناها ومن طحاها ومن سواها كله بالنون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r5.claim: One view says the soul is Adam.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r5.anchor: وفي المراد بالنفس ها هنا قولان أحدهما آدم قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r6.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r6.claim: A second view says it means all souls.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r7.claim: The meaning of fashioning the soul was discussed at 82:7.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p138#3/r7.anchor: وقد ذكرنا معنى سواها في قوله تعالى

IBNKATHIR:91:7/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:7/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:91:7/r1.claim: God created the soul balanced and upright upon the sound natural disposition, as also stated in the command to turn toward the true religion.
IBNKATHIR:91:7/r1.anchor: أي : خلقها سوية مستقيمة على الفطرة القويمة ،   كما قال تعالى : { فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًا فِطْرَةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي فَطَرَ النَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا

IBNKATHIR:91:7/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:7/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR:91:7/r2.claim: The Prophet says every newborn is born upon fitra, then parents make the child Jewish, Christian, or Magian; an animal is born whole before people mutilate it. Bukhari and Muslim transmit it.
IBNKATHIR:91:7/r2.anchor: كل مولود يولد على الفطرة ،   فأبواه يُهَوِّدانه أو يُنَصِّرانه أو يُمَجِّسانه ،

IBNKATHIR:91:7/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:7/r3.speaker: عياض بن حمار المجاشعي
IBNKATHIR:91:7/r3.claim: In a report from ʿIyad ibn Himar, God says He created His servants as upright monotheists, but devils diverted them from their religion.
IBNKATHIR:91:7/r3.anchor: إني خلقت عبادي حنفاء فجاءتهم الشياطين فاجتالتهم عن دينهم

JISHUMI:v10p7431/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r1.claim: The wāw in this sūra’s openings is the oath particle and puts following nouns in genitive; the oath particles are bāʾ, then its derivative wāw, then tāʾ, which only precedes God’s name.
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r1.anchor: الواو في قوله: (والشمس) ونظائرها واو القسم ولذلك كسر ما بعدها

JISHUMI:v10p7431/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r18.speaker: قتادة وأبي علي
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r18.claim: Qatāda and Abū ʿAlī explain the shaping of the soul as proportioning its creation, limbs, senses, and channels.
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r18.anchor: ونفس وما سواها أي: تسويتها بأن عدل خلقها وأعضاءها وحواسها ومجاريها

JISHUMI:v10p7431/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r19.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r19.claim: Al-Ḥasan supplies “God” as the maker: God built the sky, spread the earth, and fashioned the soul.
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r19.anchor: وقيل: ونفس وما سواها الله، والسماء وما بناها الله

JISHUMI:v10p7431/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r20.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r20.claim: Another construction takes the oath to be by the sky and its builder, the earth and its spreader, and the soul and its shaper.
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r20.anchor: أقسم بالسماء ومن بناها، والأرض ومن دحاها، والنفس ومن سواها

JISHUMI:v10p7431/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r22.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r22.claim: Abū Muslim connects the fāʾ of “inspired it” to “the soul and what shaped it,” meaning God shaped the soul and then inspired it.
JISHUMI:v10p7431/r22.anchor: والفاء في قوله: فألهمها عطف على قوله: (ونفس وما سواها)

KASHSHAF:91:5/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:5/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:5/r1.claim: The particle ma should be relative rather than a verbal noun: the latter weakens the sequence into fa-alhamaha; ma also conveys an adjectival meaning such as the mighty builder and wise shaper.
KASHSHAF:91:5/r1.anchor: جعلت «ما » مصدرية في قوله : { وَمَا بناها }

KASHSHAF:91:6/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:6/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:6/r1.claim: The particle ma should be relative rather than a verbal noun: the latter weakens the sequence into fa-alhamaha; ma also conveys an adjectival meaning such as the mighty builder and wise shaper.
KASHSHAF:91:6/r1.anchor: جعلت «ما » مصدرية في قوله : { وَمَا بناها }

KASHSHAF:91:7/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:7/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:7/r1.claim: The indefinite soul may be one particular soul, Adam's, or may mean every soul, with the indefinite form magnifying and multiplying its scope.
KASHSHAF:91:7/r1.anchor: أن يريد نفساً خاصة من بين النفوس وهي نفس آدم

KASHSHAF:91:7/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:7/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:7/r2.claim: The second reading takes it as every soul, like the cited indefinite expression.
KASHSHAF:91:7/r2.anchor: والثاني : أن يريد كل نفس وينكر للتكثير

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r9.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r9.claim: One view identifies the soul as Adam and its fashioner as God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r9.anchor: ومن سواها : الله تعالى , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r10.claim: Another view understands the soul as every soul.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r11.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r11.claim: On the universal-soul view, God made people equal in health and equal in punishment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r11.anchor: وسوى بينهم في العذاب جميعا , قاله ابن جريج

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r12.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r12.claim: On the universal-soul view, God proportioned and balanced the soul's creation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r12.anchor: سوى خلقها وعدل خلقها , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p282/r13.claim: A further possibility is that God endowed the soul with intellect, distinguishing it from all animals.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p342/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342/r1.claim: One analysis makes ma a verbal noun: God's building, spreading, and fashioning creation beautifully. The author rejects this because it disrupts the syntax with the following clause.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342/r1.anchor: وما مصدرية فى ﴿ والسماء وما بناها والأرض وما طحاها ونفس وما سواها ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v4p342/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342/r2.claim: The preferred analysis makes ma relative, describing the mighty Creator who built the sky and the wise One who fashioned the soul; the soul is singled out as Adam's or left indefinite to signify all souls or abundance.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342/r2.anchor: والوجه أن تكون موصولة وانما أو ثرت على من لارادة معنى الوصفية

QURTUBI-FULL:91:7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:7/r1.claim: One interpretation makes ma an infinitive: the oath is by the soul’s formation.

QURTUBI-FULL:91:7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:7/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:7/r2.claim: Another makes ma mean “the one who formed it,” namely God.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:7/r2.anchor: وقيل: المعنى ومن سواها، وهو الله عز وجل

QURTUBI-FULL:91:7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:7/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:7/r3.claim: “The soul” is interpreted either as Adam or as every individual soul.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:7/r3.anchor: وفي النفس قولان: أحدهما: آدم. الثاني: كل نفس منفوسة

QURTUBI-FULL:91:7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:7/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:7/r4.claim: Sawa means to prepare; Mujahid glosses it as forming the soul’s creation and proportioning it.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:7/r4.anchor: وسوى: بمعنى هيأ. وقال مجاهد: سواها: سوى خلقها وعدل

QURTUBI-FULL:91:7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:7/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:7/r5.claim: The preceding nouns are genitive as objects of the oath; God swears by created signs and their wonders.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:7/r5.anchor: هذه الأسماء كلها مجرورة على القسم. أقسم جل ثناؤه بخلقه لما فيه من عجائب الصنعة

QUTB-ZILAL:91:7/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:91:7/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:91:7/r1.claim: Human beings have a dual nature, formed from earthly clay and God's breathed spirit, with equal readiness for good or evil and guidance or error, and an ability to distinguish and choose.
QUTB-ZILAL:91:7/r1.anchor: مزدوج الاتجاه ونعني بكلمة مزدوج على وجه التحديد

RAZI-FULL:v31p173#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p173#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p173#3/r1.claim: Razi accepts the concern that an infinitival mā disrupts the sequence and the Qadi's concern about delaying an oath by the sky's Creator; he answers that the order stages sense before reason.
RAZI-FULL:v31p173#3/r1.anchor: والذي يخطر ببالي في الجواب عنه : أن أعظم المحسوسات هو الشمس

RAZI-FULL:v31p173#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p173#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p173#3/r2.claim: After the sun's four attributes, God is described through three acts over the sky, earth, and composite beings, represented by the soul; this guides reason from sensible creation to divine majesty.
RAZI-FULL:v31p173#3/r2.anchor: ثم ذكر ذاته المقدسة بعد ذلك ووصفها بصفات ثلاثة

RAZI-FULL:v31p174/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p174/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p174/r2.claim: God's three signs cover the physical world: simple bodies include upper heaven and lower earth, while the noblest composites are ensouled beings; the unseen is inferred from the visible.
RAZI-FULL:v31p174/r2.anchor: لأن الاستدلال على الغائب لا يمكن إلا بالشاهد

RAZI-FULL:v31p174#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p174#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p174#3/r1.claim: If nafs means the body, its proportioning is the balanced arrangement of its organs; if it means the governing faculty, God gave it hearing, sight, imagination, thought, and memory.
RAZI-FULL:v31p174#3/r1.anchor: إن حملنا النفس على الجسد ، فتسويتها تعديل أعضائها

RAZI-FULL:v31p174#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p174#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p174#3/r2.claim: One reading of the indefinite 'a soul' is the unique sacred prophetic soul, chief among composites, animals, humans, and prophets.
RAZI-FULL:v31p174#3/r2.anchor: أن يريد به نفسا خاصة من بين النفوس ، وهي النفس القدسية النبوية

RAZI-FULL:v31p174#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p174#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p174#3/r3.claim: Alternatively it means every soul; the indefinite signals multiplicity, since every animal species has a distinct soul and properties beyond human comprehension.
RAZI-FULL:v31p174#3/r3.anchor: أن يريد كل نفس ، ويكون المراد من التنكير التكثير

STUDYQURAN:91:5/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:5/r1.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:91:5/r1.claim: Some reject the rendering the One Who, saying God cannot swear by Himself; they instead read that which.
STUDYQURAN:91:5/r1.anchor: According to some, the One Who in these three verses is not appropriate, since God could not swear upon Himself

STUDYQURAN:91:5/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:5/r2.speaker: al-Qurṭubī
STUDYQURAN:91:5/r2.claim: Al-Qurṭubī prefers reading the verses as nominal phrases: its establishing, its spreading, and its fashioning.

TAB:91:7/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:7/r1.speaker: author
TAB:91:7/r1.claim: God is the one who fashioned the soul, created it, and proportioned its creation; here mā is used in place of man, ‘who.’

TAB:91:7/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:7/r2.speaker: author
TAB:91:7/r2.claim: Alternatively, mā with what follows can be a verbal noun: the oath is by the soul and its fashioning.
TAB:91:7/r2.anchor: وقد يُحتمل أن يكون معنى ذلك أيضا المصدر

TABATABAI:91:9-10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r1.claim: The soul means human souls generally, not Adam’s soul alone; a specific reading does not fit the following purification and corruption language, and there is no reason to narrow the scope.
TABATABAI:91:9-10/r1.anchor: وقيل المراد بها نفس آدم عليه السلام ولا يلائمه السياق وخاصة قوله { قد أفلح من زكاها وقد خاب من دساها }

THALABI:v10p213/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p213/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p213/r11.claim: God creates each person for one of two final destinations and prepares that person for it, as the following verses affirm.
THALABI:v10p213/r11.anchor: من كان الله سبحانه خلقه لإحدى المنزلتين يهيئه الله لها وتصديق ذلك في كتاب الله عز وجل

ASAD-NOTES:91:5#n4/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:91:5#n4/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:91:5#n4/r1.claim: Nafs here means the whole human self or personality: physical body together with the elusive life essence called soul.
ASAD-NOTES:91:5#n4/r1.anchor: denotes here the human self or personality as a whole

ASAD-NOTES:91:5#n5/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:91:5#n5/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:91:5#n5/r1.claim: Sawwa here means formed in accordance with an intended pattern, as in its earlier use at 87:2.
ASAD-NOTES:91:5#n5/r1.anchor: For this particular connotation of the verb sawwa, see note 1 on 87:2

ASAD-NOTES:91:5#n5/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:91:5#n5/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:91:5#n5/r2.claim: The interwoven bodily, emotional, and intellectual elements of human personality follow organically from contemplating the universe's grandeur as evidence of God's creative power.
ASAD-NOTES:91:5#n5/r2.anchor: the implied allusion to the extremely complex phenomenon of a life-entity

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p54/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p54/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p54/r1.claim: “What fashioned it” means the One who created and proportioned the soul’s limbs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p54/r1.anchor: المفسرون يقولون: والذي سواها، أي خلقها، وسوى أعضاها

WAHIDI-QT:91:7/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:91:7/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:91:7/r1.claim: The oath refers to the shaping of the soul's creation.

ELMALILI:91:5-10/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r7.claim: Sky and earth prepare for life and lead to the fashioning of a soul capable of perceiving its Maker and rising morally through inspiration.
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r7.anchor: kābil-i ilham bir nefsin tesviyesi kaziyyesi ile alâkadar olduğunu ihtar

ELMALILI:91:5-10/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r8.claim: The indefinite soul can be magnified as a special individual (Adam or Muhammad), a prophetic kind, or the human rational-soul kind; readings focused on Adam, Muhammad, or prophets require a special pronoun relation in the oath's response.
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r8.anchor: Şahsî mülâhaza olunduğu surette nefs-i Âdem veya nefs-i Muhammedî tebâdür eder.

ELMALILI:91:5-10/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r9.claim: A generic human rational soul best fits the response; a merely plural reading could include animal and vegetative souls unless perfection and inspiration restrict it to humans.
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r9.anchor: Tefhıym-ı cinsî murad olunduğu takdirde ise bilhassa nefs-i insânî cinsi olan nefs-i müdrike doğrudan doğru anlaşılır.

ELMALILI:91:5-10/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r10.claim: Nafs means either the entity composed of spirit and body or the spirit that governs the body.
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r10.anchor: Nefis, rûh ile bedenden mürekkeb olan zat veya bedeni müdebbir olan rûhtur.

ELMALILI:91:5-10/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r11.claim: The body's fashioning makes it ready for the breathing of spirit; the soul's fashioning arranges its organs and outward and inward powers for perfection.
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r11.anchor: Nefsin tesviyesi ise nefh-i rûh ile kemâline müsta‘id olmak üzere

ELMALILI:91:5-10/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r12.claim: Commentators differ whether ma in the three descriptions is relative, pointing to the Maker, or infinitive, naming the acts of building, spreading, and fashioning.
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r12.anchor: مَا’nin mevsûle veya masdariye olması hakkında müfessirînin iki kavli vardır.

ELMALILI:91:5-10/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r13.speaker: الفراء، الزجاج، المبرد، قتادة
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r13.claim: Farra, Zajjaj, Mubarrad, Qatada, and many others prefer the infinitive reading to avoid referring to God with ma.
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r13.anchor: Ferrâ, Zeccâc, Müberred, Katâde ve daha birçokları

ELMALILI:91:5-10/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r14.claim: Although the infinitive reading can coordinate inspiration and avoids al-Zamakhshari's objection, it leaves the verbs' agents unstated; the relative reading identifies the Maker, suits the syntax, and is preferred.
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r14.anchor: مَا’nın mevsul olması daha zâhir ve nazımda daha âhenklidir.

ELMALILI:91:5-10/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r15.claim: Using ma rather than man intensifies ambiguity and wonder about the astonishing Builder, and can introduce the unknown God to deniers by His works; the infinitive reading gives this less directly.
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r15.anchor: مَنْ yerinde مَا denilmiş olması ise iki sebepdendir.

ELMALILI:91:5-10/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r16.claim: Elmalılı chooses the relative reading in the translation while also signaling the infinitive reading in commentary; the oath moves from cosmic evidence to God's creation and inspiration of the soul.
ELMALILI:91:5-10/r16.anchor: mealde mevsûlü tercih ederek tefsirde masdariyyeye dahi işaret eyledik.

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:5-7:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:5-7:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:5-7:anmerkung/r1.claim: Although mā in 92:3 can refer to what God created, the feminine suffixes here agree with sky, earth, and soul and refer back to them; mā banāhā therefore means what each of them built or formed.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:5-7:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Während man das Pronomen mā in 92:3 auch auf das Objekt des göttlichen Schaffens anstatt auf Gott selbst beziehen kann

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:5-7:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:5-7:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:5-7:anmerkung/r2.claim: The feminine suffix -hā matches as-samāʾ, al-arḍ, and nafs, excluding the alternative that it refers to mā.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:5-7:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Das weibliche Suffix -hā stimmt im Genus mit as-samāʾ, al-ʾarḍ und nafs überein

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:7:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:7:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:7:anmerkung/r1.claim: The oath is literally by a soul and means any or every soul; 75:2 likewise swears by the soul.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:7:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Wörtlich: „Und bei einer Seele …“, im Sinne von: „und bei irgendeiner bzw. jeder beliebigen Seele …“

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:7:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:7:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:7:anmerkung/r2.claim: The verb sawwā also describes forming the human being in 75:38, 87:2, and 82:7.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:7:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Zu sawwā vgl. 75:38 (ṯumma kāna ʿalaqatan fa-ḫalaqa fa-sawwā), 87:2 (allaḏī ḫalaqa fa-sawwā)

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r1.claim: The oath’s list of opposing created phenomena moves into morality in verses 7–8 and ends with a contrastive oath naming the opposed outcomes of those moral choices.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:9-10:kommentar/r1.anchor: Die Liste gegensätzlicher Schöpfungsphänomene, die in V. 7.8 in den Bereich des Moralischen übergeht, endet schließlich mit einer ebenfalls kontrastiv gegliederte Schwuraussage

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r6.claim: Sawwā describes God’s creative formation of the soul in verse 7 and leveling in punishment in verse 14; the double use is sarcastic and links creation’s moral obligation to judgment’s enforcement of it.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r6.anchor: Die Sure charakterisiert also sowohl Gottes kreative Schöpfertätigkeit als auch seine destruktive Straftätigkeit mit demselben Verb.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p488/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p488/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p488/r7.claim: Nafs is generic, as shown by the following “inspired it” and by the contrast between whoever purifies and whoever corrupts it; its rectification completes its rational faculty.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p488/r7.anchor: ونفس وما سواها: اسم جنس، ويدل على ذلك ما بعده من قوله: فألهمها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p488/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p488/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p488/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī suggests the indefinite “a soul” might mean Adam alone; Abū Ḥayyān says this is far-fetched because the subsequent descriptions require a generic soul.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p488/r8.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: لم نكرت النفس؟ قلت: فيه وجهان: أحدها: أن يريد نفسا خاصة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p142#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p142#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p142#4/r1.claim: The soul was originated and created ready for its perfection by proportioning its outward and inward limbs and faculties.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p142#4/r1.anchor: أي أنشأها وأبدعها مستعدة لكمالها وذلك بتعديل أعضائها وقواها الظاهرة والباطنة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p142#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p142#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p142#4/r2.claim: The indefinite soul may express abundance or grandeur; if it means Adam, as some say, the reading involves a shift in reference, though the general reading better suits the oath's answer.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p142#4/r2.anchor: والتنكير للتكثير وقيل للتفخيم على أن المراد بالنفس آدم عليه السلام والأول أنسب بجواب القسم الآتي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p142#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p142#4/r3.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v30p142#4/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ, al-Zajjāj, al-Mubarrad, Qatāda, and others take ما in the three oaths as a verbal noun: building, spreading, and proportioning.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p142#4/r3.anchor: وذهب الفراء والزجاج والمبرد وقتادة وغيرهم إلى أن ما في المواضع الثلاث مصدرية أي وبنائها وطحوها وتسويتها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r4.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r4.claim: The Imam answers that the sun, the greatest perceptible object, is named with its signs of grandeur before God is described by three attributes, drawing the intellect beyond sensory things toward divine majesty.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r4.anchor: وأجاب عنه الإمام بأن أعظم المحسوسات الشسمس فذكرها الله تعالى مع أوصافها الدالة على عظمتها ثم ذكر ذاته المقدسة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r5.claim: Another proposal makes ما refer to the countless wise purposes in the making of heaven, spreading of earth, and shaping of the soul, with the actions and inspiration figuratively attributed to those purposes; Alusi finds this far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p143/r5.anchor: وجوز أن تكون ما عبارة عن الأمر الذي ينيب السماء وطحيت وسويت النفس من الحكم والمصالح التي لا تحصى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p146/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146/r5.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146/r5.claim: An esoteric mapping reads the sun as the divine essence, its brightness as the Muhammadan reality, the moon as possible-being, day as the manifest world, night as contingent existence veiling the Real, heaven as intellect, earth as body, and the camel and its drink as longing and remembrance or reflection.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146/r5.anchor: وذكر بعض أهل التأويل أن الشمس إشارة إلى ذات واجب الوجود سبحانه وتعالى وضحاها إشارة إلى الحقيقة المحمدية والقمر إشارة إلى ماهية الممكن

ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r1.speaker: بعض آخر
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r1.claim: Another esoteric scheme identifies the sun with necessary existence or the divine essence, its brightness with the first determination or its existence, the moon with fixed entities or first determination, day and night with manifestations or beauty and majesty, heaven and earth with subtle and dense worlds, and the camel with the spiritual path or the way of law.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p146#2/r1.anchor: لعيون حجبتها النقط وضحاها إشارة إلى أول التعينات بأي اسم سميته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r1.claim: God proportioned the soul’s creation and its limbs; Ata says ‘soul’ here means all that God created of jinn and humans.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p438/r1.anchor: عدل خلقها وسوى أعضاءها. قال عطاء: يريد جميع ما خلق من الجن والإنس

BAYDAWI-FULL:91:5-8/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:5-8/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:5-8/r2.claim: Making the particles source nouns would remove the agents and disrupt the grammatical sequence continued by “inspired it,” unless God is supplied implicitly.
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:5-8/r2.anchor: وجعل الماءات مصدرية يجرد الفعل عن الفاعل ويخل بنظم قوله

BAYDAWI-FULL:91:5-8/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:5-8/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:5-8/r3.claim: The indefinite soul may generalize across souls, as at 81:14, or magnify and refer specifically to Adam.
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:5-8/r3.anchor: وتنكير { نفس } للتكثير كما في قوله تعالى:

DURR-FULL:v8p528/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r8.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r8.claim: The Prophet raised his voice with the Sun and Night suras at midday so the congregation would learn their times; Ubayy asked if he had been commanded to recite them.
DURR-FULL:v8p528/r8.anchor: عن أنس: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى بهم الهاجرة فرفع صوته

DURR-FULL:v8p529/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p529/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p529/r2.claim: He says God formed the soul fully and did not diminish its creation.
DURR-FULL:v8p529/r2.anchor: {ونفس وما سواها} قال: سوى خلقها ولم ينقص منه شيئا

DURR-FULL:v8p530/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r7.claim: He says God formed the soul's creation.
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس {ونفس وما سواها} قال: سوى خلقها

ABUHAYYAN:91:7/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:7/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:91:7/r1.claim: Nafs is a generic singular, as the following reference to its inspiration confirms; the fa in the next verse orders inspiration after the adjustment that entails intellect.
ABUHAYYAN:91:7/r1.anchor: اسم جنس ،   ويدل على ذلك ما بعده

ABUHAYYAN:91:7/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:7/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:91:7/r2.claim: God's fashioning of the soul completes its intellect and capacity for reflection, explaining why inspiration follows.

ABUHAYYAN:91:7/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:7/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:91:7/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī offers the possibility that the indefinite noun means Adam's particular soul; Abū Ḥayyān finds this unlikely because the following descriptions suit a generic soul.
ABUHAYYAN:91:7/r3.anchor: قال الزمخشري : فإن قلت : لم نكرت النفس ؟ قلت : فيه وجهان

ALUSI:91:7/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:7/r1.claim: God brought the soul into being and prepared it for perfection by proportioning its outward and inward organs and powers.
ALUSI:91:7/r1.anchor: أي أنشأها وأبدعها مستعدة لكمالها وذلك بتعديل أعضائها وقواها الظاهرة والباطنة

ALUSI:91:7/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:91:7/r2.claim: One view reads the indefinite soul as magnifying the mention and identifies it as Adam.
ALUSI:91:7/r2.anchor: وقيل للتفخيم على أن المراد بالنفس آدم عليه السلام

ALUSI:91:7/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:7/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds the general reading of the soul more fitting to the oath’s answer; those identifying Adam call it istiḫdām.
ALUSI:91:7/r3.anchor: والأول أنسب بجواب القسم الآتي ومن ذهب إلى ذلك جعله من الاستخدام

ALUSI:91:7/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r4.speaker: الفراء والزجاج والمبرد وقتادة
ALUSI:91:7/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ, al-Zajjāj, al-Mubarrad, Qatāda and others take ما in the three parallel oath clauses as a verbal noun: building, spreading and fashioning.
ALUSI:91:7/r4.anchor: وذهب الفراء والزجاج والمبرد وقتادة وغيرهم إلى أن ما في المواضع الثلاث مصدرية أي وبنائها وطحوها وتسويتها

ALUSI:91:7/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI:91:7/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī objects that the source-noun reading disrupts the syntax of the following verb, leaving it coordinated to a noun and without an expressed or recoverable agent.

ALUSI:91:7/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:7/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī answers that an implicit agent is available from context, just as it is for the preceding verbs about building, spreading and fashioning.
ALUSI:91:7/r6.anchor: واعترض بأن الأخير منتقض بالأفعال السابقة أعني بناها طحاها سواها على أن دلالة السياق كافية في صحة الإضمار

ALUSI:91:7/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:7/r7.claim: He adds that coordinating a verb with a noun is not invalid, though less usual; the phrase can mean a soul and its fashioning, then its inspiration.
ALUSI:91:7/r7.anchor: عطف الفعل على الاسم ليس بفاسد وإن كان خلاف الظاهر

ALUSI:91:7/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:91:7/r8.claim: An objection says the فاء requires immediate sequence, while fashioning precedes the breathing of the soul and inspiration comes after maturity.
ALUSI:91:7/r8.anchor: واعترض هذا بأن الفاء يدل على الترتيب من غير مهملة والتسوية قبل نفخ الروح والإلهام بعد البلوغ

ALUSI:91:7/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:7/r9.claim: The reply defines fashioning as adjusting organs and faculties, including thought, and inspiration as showing how to use them along the two paths; this accompanies the soul from its fashioning and increases in manner as its faculties grow.
ALUSI:91:7/r9.anchor: وأجيب بأن التشوية تعديل الأعضاء والقوى ومنها المفكرة والإلهام عبارة عن بيان كيفية استعمالها في النجدين

ALUSI:91:7/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:7/r10.claim: The objection about sequence is not decisive: such ordering may be customary rather than literal, and the same objection burdens both analyses.
ALUSI:91:7/r10.anchor: على أن المهلة في نحوها عرفي وقد يعد متعقباً دون تراخ ثم أنه مشترك الإلزام

ALUSI:91:7/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r11.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI:91:7/r11.claim: Al-Ṭībī argues that the finely balanced cadence requires matching clauses and rules out coordinating the verb this way; al-Ālūsī says this assumes the following phrase is an independent sentence.
ALUSI:91:7/r11.anchor: ولا معنى لقول الطيبي النظم السري يوجب موافقة القرائن فلا يجوز ونفس وتسويتها فألهمها الله

ALUSI:91:7/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r12.speaker: القاضي عبد الجبار
ALUSI:91:7/r12.claim: Al-Qāḍī ʿAbd al-Jabbār insists on the source-noun reading to avoid placing an oath by created things before God’s oath by Himself.
ALUSI:91:7/r12.anchor: وأبى القاضي عبد الجبار إلا المصدرية دون الموصولية قال لما يلزم منها تقديم الإقسام بغير الله تعالى على إقسامه

ALUSI:91:7/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r13.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI:91:7/r13.claim: Al-Imām replies that the sun, greatest among sensible things, is described first with four signs of its greatness, then God names Himself with three attributes, drawing reason from the sensible world toward divine majesty.
ALUSI:91:7/r13.anchor: وأجاب عنه الإمام بأن أعظم المحسوسات الشمس فذكرها الله تعالى مع أوصافها الأربعة الدالة على عظمها

ALUSI:91:7/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:7/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:7/r14.claim: A further possibility makes ما the cosmic order of countless wisdoms behind the sky, earth and soul, with the actions and inspiration predicated of it metaphorically; al-Ālūsī dismisses this.
ALUSI:91:7/r14.anchor: وجوز أن تكون ما عبارة عن الأمر الذي له بنيت السماء وطحيت الأرض وسويت النفس من الحكم والمصالح

ALUSI:91:8/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:8/r1.claim: God brought the soul into being and prepared it for perfection by proportioning its outward and inward organs and powers.
ALUSI:91:8/r1.anchor: أي أنشأها وأبدعها مستعدة لكمالها وذلك بتعديل أعضائها وقواها الظاهرة والباطنة

ALUSI:91:8/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:91:8/r2.claim: One view reads the indefinite soul as magnifying the mention and identifies it as Adam.
ALUSI:91:8/r2.anchor: وقيل للتفخيم على أن المراد بالنفس آدم عليه السلام

ALUSI:91:8/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:91:8/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds the general reading of the soul more fitting to the oath’s answer; those identifying Adam call it istiḫdām.
ALUSI:91:8/r3.anchor: والأول أنسب بجواب القسم الآتي ومن ذهب إلى ذلك جعله من الاستخدام

ALUSI:91:8/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:8/r4.speaker: الفراء والزجاج والمبرد وقتادة

BAGHAWI:91:7/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:91:7/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:91:7/r1.claim: God proportioned the soul's creation and made its limbs even.

BAGHAWI:91:7/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:91:7/r2.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI:91:7/r2.claim: ʿAta takes “a soul” to mean all that God created of jinn and humans.
BAGHAWI:91:7/r2.anchor: قال عطاء : يريد جميع ما خلق من الجن والإنس

BAYDAWI:91:7/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:91:7/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:91:7/r1.claim: Taking the repeated mā particles as infinitival leaves the verbs without stated agents and disrupts the syntax with the next verse; one must understand God's name as implicit.
BAYDAWI:91:7/r1.anchor: وجعل الماءات مصدرية يجرد الفعل عن الفاعل ويخل بنظم قوله فألهمها فجورها وتقواها

BAYDAWI:91:7/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:91:7/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:91:7/r2.claim: The indefinite “soul” may indicate abundance, as in the verse “a soul will know what it brought,” or may magnify it; the referent is Adam's soul.
BAYDAWI:91:7/r2.anchor: وتنكير نفس للتكثير كما في قوله تعالى علمت نفس أو للتعظيم والمراد نفس آدم

BIQAI:91:7/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:7/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:7/r1.claim: After hinting at souls for people of insight, the text speaks explicitly for those below them; a soul gathers the whole created world within it.
BIQAI:91:7/r1.anchor: ولما أتم الإشارة إلى النفوس لأهل البصائر ،   صرح بالعبارة لمن دونهم

BIQAI:91:7/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:7/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:7/r2.claim: God fashioned the soul in a supremely wise order, balancing its limbs, substances, accidents, meanings, and contrary humors; reflecting on it leads to its Maker and to self-reform.
BIQAI:91:7/r2.anchor: ولما كانت النفوس أعجب ما في الكون وأجمع ،   عبر فيها بالتسوية حثاً على تدبر أمرها للاستدلال على مبدعها

BIQAI:91:7/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:7/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:91:7/r3.claim: The implied oath response is that God stamped souls with differing dispositions and prepared them for purification or corruption through the capacity and choice given to them, urging purification and belief in resurrection.
BIQAI:91:7/r3.anchor: وقد أرشد السياق والسباق واللحاق إلى أن جواب القسم مقدر تقديره : لقد طبع سبحانه وتعالى نفوسكم على طبائع متباينة

BIQAI:91:7/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:91:7/r4.speaker: الأستاذ أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:91:7/r4.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links the oath to human hardship and the guidance of 90:10 and 76:3: people have acquired capacity, not independent agency, and the sūra contrasts those who choose guidance with those who follow desire.
BIQAI:91:7/r4.anchor: وقال الأستاذ أبو جعفر ابن الزبير : لما تقدم في سورة البلد تعريفه تعالى بما خلق فيه الإنسان من الكبد

DURR:91:7/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:91:7/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:91:7/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God proportioned the soul’s creation.
DURR:91:7/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن ابن عباس { ونفس وما سواها } قال : سوى خلقها .

IBNASHUR:91:7/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:7/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:7/r1.claim: Al-nafs means the human self or person, as in the address to the tranquil soul.
IBNASHUR:91:7/r1.anchor: ذات الإِنسان كما تقدم عند قوله تعالى :  { يا أيتها

IBNASHUR:91:7/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:7/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:7/r2.claim: The indefinite noun marks a species, so by contextual indication it comprehensively includes every soul.
IBNASHUR:91:7/r2.anchor: وتنكير « نفس » للنوعية أي جنس النفس فيعم كل نفس عموماً بالقرينة

IBNASHUR:91:7/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:7/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:7/r3.claim: Smoothing the soul means creating it evenly, without disparity in its formation.
IBNASHUR:91:7/r3.anchor: وتسوية النفس :  خلقها سواء ،  أي غير متفاوتة الخَلْق

IBNASHUR:91:7/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:91:7/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:91:7/r4.claim: The three ma clauses may be masdariyya; the oath then invokes effects of divine power: raising heaven, spreading earth, and forming humanity.
IBNASHUR:91:7/r4.anchor: إمّا مصدرية يؤوَّلُ الفعل بعدها بمصدر فالقسم بأمور من آثار قدرة الله تعالى وهي صفات الفعل الإلهية

IBNATIYYA:91:7/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:91:7/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:91:7/r1.claim: The sworn-by soul is a generic noun; its fashioning perfects its intellect and reflection, which the following verse's fāʾ links to inspiration.
IBNATIYYA:91:7/r1.anchor: والنفس التي أقسم بها ، اسم الجنس ، وتسويتها إكمال عقلها ونظرها

MAWARDI:91:7/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:7/r1.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI:91:7/r1.claim: The soul is Adam, and the one who fashioned him is God.
MAWARDI:91:7/r1.anchor: أحدهما : آدم ، ومن سواها : الله تعالى ، قاله الحسن

MAWARDI:91:7/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:7/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:91:7/r2.claim: Another view takes the soul to mean every soul.

MAWARDI:91:7/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:7/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI:91:7/r3.claim: On the universal reading, God made souls equal in health and equal in punishment.
MAWARDI:91:7/r3.anchor: أحدهما : سوى بينهم في الصحة ، وسوى بينهم في العذاب جميعا ، قاله ابن جريج

MAWARDI:91:7/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:7/r4.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI:91:7/r4.claim: On the universal reading, God formed each soul and proportioned its creation.
MAWARDI:91:7/r4.anchor: الثاني : سوى خلقها وعدل خلقها ، قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI:91:7/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:7/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI:91:7/r5.claim: A further possibility is that God fashioned the soul with reason, which gives it distinction over all animals.
MAWARDI:91:7/r5.anchor: سوّاها بالعقل الذي فضّلها به على جميع الحيوانات

NASAFI:91:7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:91:7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:91:7/r1.claim: A masdariyya “ma” would mean the soul's fashioning; some say it is fashioned in the best form, but Nasafi says this disrupts the syntax with the next verse.
NASAFI:91:7/r1.anchor: أي وبنائها وطحوها أي بسطها وتسوية خلقها في أحسن صورة عند البعض وليس بالوجه لقوله { فَأَلْهَمَهَا }

NASAFI:91:7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:91:7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:91:7/r2.claim: Nasafi prefers relative “ma” over “man” to express description: the powerful one who built the sky and the wise one who fashioned the soul.
NASAFI:91:7/r2.anchor: والوجه أن تكون موصولة وإنما أوثرت على «من » لإرادة معنى الوصفية كأنه قيل

NASAFI:91:7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:91:7/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:91:7/r3.claim: The indefinite “a soul” may mean Adam in particular or all souls, with indefiniteness conveying abundance as in 69:2.
NASAFI:91:7/r3.anchor: وإنما نكرت النفس لأنه أراد نفساً خاصة من بين النفوس وهي نفس آدم

QURTUBI:91:7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:7/r1.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:91:7/r1.claim: One parsing takes mā as a verbal noun, so the phrase means the soul and its fashioning.
QURTUBI:91:7/r1.anchor: قيل : المعنى وتسويتها . " فما " : بمعنى المصدر

QURTUBI:91:7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:7/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:91:7/r2.claim: Another parsing takes mā as meaning who, referring to God as the one who fashioned the soul.
QURTUBI:91:7/r2.anchor: وقيل : المعنى ومن سواها ، وهو الله عز وجل

QURTUBI:91:7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:7/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:91:7/r3.claim: The soul may refer either to Adam or to every human soul.
QURTUBI:91:7/r3.anchor: وفي النفس قولان : أحدهما آدم . الثاني : كل نفس منفوسة

QURTUBI:91:7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:7/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:91:7/r4.claim: Sawwā means prepared or made ready.

QURTUBI:91:7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:7/r5.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI:91:7/r5.claim: Mujāhid glosses the phrase as fashioning and proportioning the soul's creation.
QURTUBI:91:7/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد : سواها : سوى خلقها وعدل

QURTUBI:91:7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:7/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI:91:7/r6.claim: All these nouns are genitive as objects of the oath.
QURTUBI:91:7/r6.anchor: وهذه الأسماء كلها مجرورة على القسم

QURTUBI:91:7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:91:7/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI:91:7/r7.claim: God swears by His creation because its wondrous workmanship points to Him.
QURTUBI:91:7/r7.anchor: أقسم جل ثناؤه بخلقه لما فيه من عجائب الصنعة الدالة عليه

RAZI:91:7/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:7/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:91:7/r1.claim: If nafs means the body, its fashioning is the proportioning of its limbs, as anatomy shows.

RAZI:91:7/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:7/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:91:7/r2.claim: If nafs means the governing faculty, its fashioning is by giving it powers of hearing, sight, imagination, thought, and memory, as psychology shows.
RAZI:91:7/r2.anchor: فتسويتها إعطاؤها القوى الكثيرة كالقوة السامعة والباصرة والمخيلة والمفكرة والمذكورة

RAZI:91:7/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:7/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:91:7/r3.claim: One explanation of the indefinite noun is that it singles out the prophetic, sanctified soul as chief over the world of composite beings.
RAZI:91:7/r3.anchor: أن يريد به نفسا خاصة من بين النفوس

RAZI:91:7/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:7/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:91:7/r4.claim: This view reasons that every multiplicity has a chief: composites are headed by animals, animal kinds by humans, human kinds by prophets, and the prophets by one supreme leader.
RAZI:91:7/r4.anchor: كل كثرة ، فلابد فيها من واحد يكون هو الرئيس

RAZI:91:7/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:7/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:91:7/r5.claim: Alternatively, the indefinite noun means every soul and conveys abundance, as in “each soul shall know what it has brought.”
RAZI:91:7/r5.anchor: أن يريد كل نفس ، ويكون المراد من التنكير التكثير

RAZI:91:7/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:91:7/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:91:7/r6.claim: Souls belong to innumerable animal kinds; each is distinct in its defining qualities, and human understanding cannot grasp even the few qualities of fleas and mosquitoes, much less God’s secrets.
RAZI:91:7/r6.anchor: ولكل نوع نفس مخصوصة متميزة عن سائرها بالفضل

RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r1.claim: Razi presents an affinity principle: pure, luminous human souls join pure spirits that aid virtue, while corrupt, dark souls join evil spirits that aid sin and aggression.
RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r1.anchor: الجنسية علة الضم فالنفوس البشرية الطاهرة النورانية تنضم إليها تلك الأرواح الطاهرة النورانية

RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r2.speaker: الفريق الثالث
RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r2.claim: The third group denies lower spirits but affirms separate celestial spirits, which it describes as high, powerful, and differing in their essences and natures.
RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r2.anchor: الفريق الثالث : وهم الذين ينكرون وجود الأرواح السفلية ولكنهم أثبتوا وجود الأرواح المجردة الفلكية

RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r3.speaker: الفريق الثالث
RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r3.claim: This group analogizes each celestial soul's assigned sphere to a human soul's body: each first attaches to its heart or planet, then its influence spreads through the whole body or sphere and world.
RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r3.anchor: فكما أن لكل روح من الأرواح البشرية بدنا معينا فكذلك لكل روح من الأرواح الفلكية بدن معين

RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r4.speaker: الفريق الثالث
RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r4.claim: As subtle spirits from heart and brain travel through arteries and nerves to distribute life, sensation, and motion throughout the body, planetary radial rays carry planetary influence to every region of the world.
RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r4.anchor: تتأدى في الشرايين والأعصاب إلى أجزاء البدن ويصل بهذا الطريق قوة الحياة والحس والحركة

RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r5.speaker: الفريق الثالث
RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r5.claim: The bodily faculties of nutrition, growth, generation, and sensation are outcomes of the governing soul; similarly planetary rays generate particular human souls, such as Zayd and ʿAmr, as offspring of planetary souls.
RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r5.anchor: فتكون هذه القوى كالنتائج والأولاد لجوهر النفس المدبرة لكلية البدن

RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r6.speaker: الفريق الثالث
RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r6.claim: Since planetary souls differ in essence, souls associated with Saturn form a mutually homogeneous group marked by affection, while differing in nature from souls associated with Jupiter.
RAZI-FULL:v1p72/r6.anchor: فتكون النفوس المنتسبة إلى روح زحل متجانسة متشاركة ويحصل بينها محبة ومودة

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p285/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p285/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p285/r1.claim: ما and من share an origin: من is used for people, while ما is used for nonhuman things.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p285/r1.anchor: ما ومن، أصلهما واحد، فجعلت من للناس، وما لغير الناس.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p285/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p285/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p285/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda takes ما in these passages, including «ونفس وما سواها», to mean من, “who.”
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p285/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة في قوله تعالى وما خلق الذكر والأنثى (3) [الليل: 3] : أي ومن خلق الذكر والأنثى.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p285/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p285/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p285/r3.claim: Abū ʿAmr says ما means “that which”; Meccans use the same relative pronoun in their saying when they hear thunder.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p285/r3.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو: هي بمعنى (الذي) . قال: وأهل مكة يقولون إذا سمعوا صوت الرعد: سبحان ما سبحت له.

BURHAN:v2p5/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p5/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p5/r7.claim: In affirmative contexts, an indefinite singular can have a generalized individual reading; adding كل makes the generality explicit, as in كل نفس.
BURHAN:v2p5/r7.anchor: وفي سياق الإثبات بعموم القلة المقتضى

BURHAN:v3p42/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p42/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p42/r3.claim: Divine oaths may name God, His acts, or created things; they may be explicit, marked by an oath lām, or implicit in meaning.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r6.claim: Mā can mean “who” or “the one that” in oaths; some group it with the relative sense.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r6.anchor: والسابع : بمعنى ' من ' . ومنه قوله تعالى في الشمس

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba reports Abū ʿAmr’s view that mā in the oaths means “that which.”
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r7.anchor: فذكر ابن قتيبة : عن أبي عمرو أنه قال : هي بمعنى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r8.speaker: أهل مكة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r8.claim: Meccans say on hearing thunder, “Glory to the One whom it glorifies,” illustrating mā as a relative form.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p566/r8.anchor: وأهل مكة يقولون إذا سمعوا الرعد : سبحان ما سبحت له

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r1.claim: God swears by the soul and its fashioning, then teaches it to recognize righteous and wicked deeds, a knowledge shared by ignorant and learned alike.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p205/r1.anchor: أقسم بالنفس وخلقه لها ثم قال: فألهمها فجورها وتقواها، أي: فهمها أعمال البر وأعمال الفجور، حتى عرف ذلك الجاهل والعاقل

ALUSI:91:11/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:91:11/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI:91:11/r9.claim: ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn reports two men of Muzayna asking whether people’s deeds were decreed beforehand or established through prophetic teaching; the Prophet answered that they were decreed and had already passed, citing 91:7–8. The cited collections are al-Bukhārī, Muslim, and Abū Dāwūd.
ALUSI:91:11/r9.anchor: عن عمران بن حصين أن رجلين من مزينة أتيا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالا يا رسول الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p340/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p340/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p340/r9.claim: Taswiyah means straightening and making creation precise; restoring the fingertips finely is a metonym for creating them, since nothing is made well-proportioned without being recreated.
